schemaVersion.description: The major version of this contract

id.description: 64 lowercase hex digits. Opaque to readers

producer.description: A stable name for the suite or tool. With the check id, environment and parameters it picks the slot a layer fills

recordedAtMs.description: When the checks ran, in epoch milliseconds. The newest completed result wins its slot

sha.description: The commit the checks ran against. Provenance only; it never partitions a report

runUrl.description: Where to read the CI run that produced it

environment.description: The client that was checked: desktop-web, mobile-web, ios, android, or any other lowercase name

parameters.description: Other choices that make a result its own slot, such as a device size

freshness.description: `modified`: recorded from a checkout with uncommitted changes. `unknown`: origin not captured

run.description: The execution this layer belongs to, when the producer names one (a local or manual run without a CI run URL). Grouping and display only; it never partitions a report or decides a result

id.description: The execution's identity within a project, chosen by the producer: a UUID, a timestamped name. Layers with the same id are one run; it never changes after it is recorded

title.description: A human name for the run. Presentation only: it is not part of the identity and does not hide the commit or `freshness`

startedAtMs.description: When the execution started, epoch milliseconds

endedAtMs.description: When the execution ended, epoch milliseconds

fingerprint.description: Identity of the spec text the layer was recorded against, to warn when the spec changed since

sha.description: Repeats the layer sha; readers use the layer

kind.description: An open category: behavior, performance, accessibility… A new kind needs no change to a reader

id.description: The check's stable identity within its producer. The same check must keep the same id in every layer, or layers cannot replace one another

detail.description: Why it failed, or what was measured

specPath.description: The spec this check belongs to, relative to the repository, such as specs/join.feature

limit.description: The allowance. A measurement over it is reported, and never fails the check by itself

durationMs.description: How long the check took, when the producer measured it

recordingExpectation.description: `required`: expect a video of this check, and report whether it was published. `not-applicable`: intentionally unrecorded. Absent: no expectation. Never changes the check's status

tags.description: Free labels to filter and group by: smoke, slow, flaky…

labels.description: Facts about the result, not part of its identity: owner, severity, browser, os, build. Unlike `parameters` they never split a result into another slot

rel.description: Why it is linked, in an open vocabulary: issue, run, trace, docs, source…

id.description: Lets another attachment, step or annotation refer to this one

contentType.description: An IANA media type. Absent means application/octet-stream

bundleKey.description: The key of its bytes in the layer

uri.description: Where else to read it: an https URL, or a path a host understands

omitted.description: Why the producer did not include its bytes, in an open vocabulary: too-large, not-found, not-allowed, over-budget, policy… Present on a metadata-only attachment, so a reader can tell "left out" from "never recorded"

scope.description: What this one attachment (usually a recording) does and does not show. Overrides the scope of its attempt, check, part and layer as a whole

surface.description: Where the product ran, in an open vocabulary: `browser`, `native-app`, `api`, `cli`…

deviceKind.description: What it ran on, in an open vocabulary: `simulator`, `emulator`, `physical`, `virtual-machine`, `desktop`… A simulator and a physical phone stay distinct values; they are filtered separately

syntheticData.description: True: the data was made up for the run. False: real data. Absent: unknown

dependencies.description: Whether what the product talks to was `scripted` (replies fixed in advance), `live` or `mixed`. An open vocabulary; absent is unknown

audioCaptured.description: True: the recording has real audio. False: it is silent. Absent: unknown

pacing.description: How time ran, in an open vocabulary: `paced` (slowed or scripted for a viewer), `real-time`. Absent: unknown

asserted.description: The boundaries the result actually asserts. Activity visible in a recording beyond them is not verified behavior

limitations.description: Known limits of what this evidence shows, in the producer's words

declaredBy.description: Who or what made this declaration: a tool, a team, a person

verified.description: The names of the fields above (`surface`, `deviceKind`, `syntheticData`, `dependencies`, `audioCaptured`, `pacing`) that something independent of the producer checked. Every other field is only declared

provenance.description: Where the declaration comes from and how to check it: a document, a CI step, a device log

rel.description: Why it is linked, in an open vocabulary: issue, run, trace, docs, source…

tags.description: Free labels of this one attachment, such as `demo`: shown as `#demo`, searchable, and normalized by `normalizeTag` (a leading `#` and letter case never matter). Unlike the tags of a check they say nothing about its result

poster.description: The `id` of an attachment that stands for this one before it is opened

captions.description: The `id`s of attachments (WebVTT, SRT) that caption this one
